history.summary: A cave temple dedicated to Lord Shiva as Adumalleshwara ('the dancing form of Malleshwara', per local gloss) set in the rugged forested hills of Chitradurga. The sanctum is embedded in a natural cave housing a lingam believed to be swayambhu; a perennial spring flows from the mouth of the Nandi idol (the temple's main attraction), and a stepped tank (pushkarini) lies opposite the shrine. Local tradition attributes the shrine to the Nayakas of Chitradurga, though its exact age is unrecorded and uninscribed. The temple sits within a reserve forest/eco-park with a small forest-department mini-zoo (spotted deer, peacocks, rabbits, birds) adjoining it, making it a popular picnic and nature-walk spot as well as a place of worship. Opening hours are CONFLICTED between sources (see visitor_information).

name: Adumalleshwara Temple
town_description: Chitradurga, in central Karnataka about 200 km north-west of Bengaluru, is famed for its massive hill fort - the 'Stone Fort' (Yelu Suttina Kote, fort of seven walls) built between the 10th and 18th centuries by the Rashtrakutas, Chalukyas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara and finally the Nayakas of Chitradurga, whose last ruler Madakari Nayaka fell to Hyder Ali in 1779. The fort houses eighteen temples and is associated with the heroism of Onake Obavva and the Bhima-Hidimba legend.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, approx. 200 km (verify); nearest air access is via Bengaluru.
travel.road: Around 4-5 km from Chitradurga town on Aadumalleshwara Road, on the NH-48 Bengaluru-Davangere corridor; reachable by auto, bus and private vehicle.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the climate is cooler and ideal for the surrounding forest walk. Early morning or late afternoon are the quietest times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): Justdial lists temple hours as 6:00 AM-1:00 PM daily; MakeMyTrip states the temple is accessible 9:30 AM-5:30 PM (matching the adjoining zoo's 9:30 AM-5:30 PM hours; zoo closed Tuesdays). No authoritative temple timings found online.
